IdentityA hunter and tracker of the wild places who knows its chosen enemies, reads the land and fights with blade or bow at the edge of civilisation.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

LvlYou gain

Class Abilities

1st Level

Hunter's Edge

  • Effect: Your weapon hits deal +1 damage. Improves to +2 at 7th level and +3 at 15th.

Marked Prey

  • Effect: Once per encounter, before you roll an attack, mark a creature you can see.
  • The mark lasts the encounter, on one creature at a time.
  • While it is your marked prey, you have Advantage on your first attack roll each round against it and on Tracking checks to follow it; the Advantage to track it lasts until you next rest.
  • 4th: you may use Marked Prey twice per encounter, on different creatures.
  • 5th: if your marked prey dies or drops to 0 HP (a solo counts when it drops to 0 HP in a phase), you may mark a new creature you can see at once, or the same solo in its next phase, without spending a use of Marked Prey.

Woodcraft

  • Effect: You are Trained in Survival, Tracking, Set Snares and Climb (Book II), on top of your starting skills, and Master in Tracking from 5th level. You read tracks (a trail's condition and the creature type from 3rd level), find food and shelter for yourself without a check and for 2d4 others on a Moderate check, and set and disarm wilderness traps (see Ranger Traps).
  • Hide and Move Silently (Dexterity): in natural terrain your pace sets the roll, as for the Rogue's Hide and Move Silently: half speed or less, Advantage; normal speed, a normal roll; running or charging, Disadvantage.
  • In natural terrain you count as Hidden even on a result of 12 to 14.
  • From 5th level you may attempt both together, at quarter speed, with Disadvantage on both.
  • Delay/Neutralise Poison (Wisdom): For natural poisons familiar to you (those of your home region and your favoured enemies). On a successful check: delay the poison's effects for 1 hour per level (no action, 1 attempt only).
    • If the roll exceeds the needed total by 6 or more: neutralise the poison entirely (effects already suffered are not reversed)

Hunter's Tricks

  • Effect: On one hit of your choice against your marked prey each round, choose one: Hamstring (its speed is halved until the end of its next turn), Pin (until the end of its next turn, it can't move away from you without a Reflex save against your Class Save DC) or Expose (the next ally to attack it has Advantage).
  • From 8th level, your Quarry Strike's hit can carry a trick too.
  • This combines with the Favoured Enemy die.

2nd Level

Find Passage

  • Effect: In wild terrain of a kind you have travelled before, difficult terrain doesn't slow you: it costs you no extra movement and doesn't drop your travel pace. A party you guide keeps its travel pace too.

Ranger Traps

You carry the makings for your traps.

  • You may have up to three set at once; a trap lasts until it is sprung or you leave the area (a day at most).
  • A trap fills one 5ft space; a snare or pit holds a creature up to Large, and a pit needs earth to dig.
  • A set trap is hidden: a creature spots it only if its passive awareness meets your Class Save DC, and a creature that searches finds it with a Wisdom check against the same DC.
  • A creature that steps into a trap's space springs it and makes the save against your Class Save DC.
TrapFromSetEffect on a failed save
Snare2nd1 roundReflex: 1d6 bludgeoning and Restrained, hung by a foot, until it or a creature beside it uses an action to cut it free
Spike2nd1 roundReflex: 2d6 piercing and speed halved until the end of its next turn; half damage on a success
Smoke3rd1 roundNo save: thick smoke fills a 20ft radius, heavily obscured, until the end of the encounter
Pit5th10 minutesReflex: falls into a staked pit, 4d6 piercing and Prone; climbing out takes all its movement
Glue7th1 roundReflex: Restrained; it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns
Great jaw trap10th1 minuteReflex: 8d6 piercing and Restrained; it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, or a creature beside it frees it with an action; half damage and not Restrained on a success

3rd Level

Favoured Enemy

  • Effect: Choose a creature type from Monsters & Treasure (aberration, beast, celestial, construct, dragon, elemental, fey, fiend, giant, humanoid, monstrosity, ooze, plant or undead) as your favoured enemy; the GM may ask that it be one your character has met before.
    • Against a favoured enemy, one hit of your choice each round deals an extra weapon damage die and ignores its Resistance; it has Disadvantage on Hide checks against you, and the first attack a favoured enemy makes against you each round has Disadvantage.
    • You have Advantage on checks to track it and to neutralise its poisons.
  • More enemies: you choose another favoured enemy at 6th and 9th level, and two more at 15th, five in all.
  • Changing one: by spending a Downtime Phase studying a creature type (its lore, its tracks, a carcass or a captive, as the GM allows), you may swap one of your favoured enemies for it.

Advanced Tracking (Wisdom)

  • Effect: After a successful track check, determine accurately the number in the tracked party, their make-up (war band, hunting party, etc.), whether well or lightly armed, their speed, and their habits.
  • A second successful Wisdom check can predict their intended direction of travel; a third can identify their specific destination

5th Level

Quarry Strike

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, make one additional weapon attack as part of it, with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex). No Disadvantage against your marked prey.

6th Level

Apex Predator

  • Effect: Once per day, when you use Marked Prey, for the encounter your marked prey has Disadvantage on Hide checks against you, its speed is halved while it moves away from you, and you know where it is while it's within 60ft; a creature that turns invisible stays marked.

9th Level

Survival Instincts (Wisdom)

  • Effect: You have Advantage on checks to avoid being surprised: when the GM checks for Surprise, add 5 to your passive awareness (see Surprise Rounds in The Arneyan Codex). From 15th level you are never surprised in the wilderness.

10th Level

Relentless Hunter

  • Effect: Every hit against your marked prey deals an extra weapon damage die and ignores its Resistance. It combines with Hunter's Tricks and with the Favoured Enemy die. This is the Ranger's exception to one damage die a round.

Renown: Name

  • Effect: Your deeds are known. Title: Warden of the Wilds. In any wild land, a forester, trapper or guide will join your party for a journey for food alone. Your first follower, a scout, joins you.

13th Level

Read the Land

  • Effect: An hour's study of the land tells you what has passed within a mile of you in the last week: its kind, roughly how many, and which way they went.

15th Level

  • Dexterity Bonus: permanent +1 Dexterity. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).
  • Renown: Holding: you may found a hunting lodge as your Holding (see Your Holding (15th) in Keeps & Kingdoms).
  • Hunter's Edge, Favoured Enemy and Survival Instincts improve, as their entries say.

17th Level

Beast Lore

  • Effect: You know the lairs, habits and seasons of every beast and monster in a region you have travelled.

20th Level

Peerless Hunter

  • Effect: Apex Predator applies every time you use Marked Prey, with no daily limit.
  • You have Advantage on every attack roll against your marked prey, not only the first each round, and on checks to track, corner or finish it.
  • Once per encounter, one hit against your marked prey deals maximum damage, extra dice included.

Renown: The Lodge

  • Effect: You may found a lodge (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex), matching Keeps & Kingdoms' Ranger lodge; each season 1d6 scouts and one 1st-level Ranger join it. While you hold it, you can't be surprised within a day's travel of it, nor can anyone travelling with you.

Kits: Ranger Traditions

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Ranger folder. Drag one onto your character.

Choose one Kit at character creation: how you hunt and where you learned it.

  • Each kit gives features at 1st, 5th and 9th level, and reshapes one of your base features, as its Reshapes line says.
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.
